Question: Why do people say dating sucks if they are in a relationship?
Answer: You know, that’s actually a fascinating question. I’ve heard a lot of people say “dating sucks,” and I’ve asked a lot of people why they think dating sucks, and the answers I get always leave me feeling like I’m talking to some strange alien visitor in a human suit, or perhaps I am a strange alien visitor in a human suit…because man, what they call “dating” and what I call “dating” ain’t on the same planet. Consistently, time after time, year after year, by far the most common answer I get to “why does dating suck?” is: I can’t be myself. I always have to be on my best behavior. I feel like I’m auditioning. And I’m like… Like, I can’t even begin to wrap my head around that. Like, why would you even go into a date from that perspective? Put on a show to try to get your date to like you? The function of a date is to find out if the two of you are compatible and mutually interested in exploring a relationship. Show up with your authentic self, be open without expectation, see if you both come away with the same desire. If you do, awesome! Keep dating. If you don’t, awesome! You’ve learned the two of you aren’t a good match. I’ve had first dates that have gone splendidly. When we met in person, my Talespinner took me to a lovely rum bar where we sat and talked and sipped rum and worked on our novel together, then we had our first kiss beside a fountain. Simple, nothing elaborate, nothing exciting, but it’s one of my all-time favorite first dates ever. I’ve had first dates where I’ve left feeling naah, not gonna work. I’ve had first dates where I’ve left thinking “wow, she’s awesome, I really would like to keep dating her” and she left feeling naah, not gonna work. That’s all okay. Go in open to things working out but not counting on or invested in any particular outcome, and you don’t feel like you’re putting on a show or auditioning or trying to win someone over or whatever. It’s genuinely okay if the answer is no. (I actually think this is related to the difference between an abundance mindset and a starvation mindset of love and connection, and putting on an act because you feel you have to make this date work is one of those self-sabotaging things that leads to dates not working and reinforces a starvation mindset, but that’s a whole conversation outside the scope of this answer.) There’s a bunch of other stuff too: “you need money to date” (you really really don’t, believe me), “dating is a numbers game” (well, maybe if you didn’t think of people as commodities that would change?), “I can’t seem to find anyone who fits into my life” (have you given any thought whatsoever to how you might fit into her life? Any at all?)…but yeah, dating-as-audition? That’s just…I don’t even know what the hell that is.
